newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Britons injured in Japan auto crash.
newsitem.headline: Two Britons injured in Japan auto crash.

text.p: Two Britons were seriously injured in a a road accident near the Suzuka motor racing circuit in western Japan, the venue of Japanese Grand Prix motor race, police said on Saturday.
A police spokesman told Reuters that Chris Heathorn and Adam Chapman were injured when the van they were travelling in rolled over as it tried to avoid hitting a car coming out of a branch road.

The two work for a restaurant company that is providing foods for Formula One racing teams throughout the season. The van was carrying six restaurant staffers -- five Britons, including Heathorn and Chapman, and an Australian.
The spokesman quoted doctors' statements as saying that Chapman, 40, suffered serious head injuries in the accident and was still unconscious.
But Heathorn regained consciousness early on Saturday despite suffering a head injury, the spokesman said.
The remaining four received facial injuries and were admitted to hospitals in Suzuka and nearby Yokkaichi city.
A police spokesman said he did not know the home towns of Heathorn and Chapman.

The Japanese Grand Prix, the last leg of the 16-race Formula One world championship series, is currently under way at the circuit and Sunday's race will decide this year's world motor racing Formula One champion.
